extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / differential geometry studying Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and theorems giving precise non-collapsing criteria for solutions of the Ricci flow (Perelman's no local collapsing I, I′, II) and a Cheeger-type C^∞_loc compactness/convergence theorem for sequences of marked Riemannian manifolds with local curvature and injectivity radius control.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on scale r (Definition 3.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let κ, r > 0 and gij(t), 0 ≤ t < T, be a solution to the Ricci flow on an n-dimensional manifold M. The solution gij(t) is κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on the scale r if whenever |Rm|(x,t) ≤ r^{-2} for all x ∈ B_{t0}(x0,r) and t ∈ [t0 − r^2, t0], we have Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bt0(x0,r) is the geodesic ball centered at x0 with respect to the metric g(t0). This is the basic quantitative non-collapsing condition used throughout the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem I (Theorem 3.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any initial metric gij on a compact n-manifold M, let gij(t) be the solution to the Ricci flow on M starting at gij and existing on [0,T). Then there exist positive constants κ and ρ0 (depending on the initial metric and T) such that for any t0 ∈ [0,T) and any point x0 ∈ M the solution is κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on all scales less than ρ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem gives a local injectivity radius/volume lower bound in terms of local curvature bounds; it is emphasized as crucial because it survives the surgeries used later. The proof uses Perelman's reduced volume monotonicity and a contradiction/blow-up argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem I′ (Theorem 3.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose M is compact and gij(t), 0 ≤ t < T, is a solution to the Ricci flow. There exists κ > 0 (depending only on the initial metric and T) such that for any (x0,t0) and any 0 < r ≤ √T, if the scalar curvature satisfies R(x,t0) ≤ r^{-2} for all x ∈ B_{t0}(x0,r), then Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strengthening where the curvature bound hypothesis is replaced by a scalar curvature bound on the geodesic ball. The proof uses Perelman's µ-functional and test functions with cutoffs; details include constructing a test function f and bounding W(g,f,τ) to extract a volume lower bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic Laplacian comparison / distance evolution inequalities (Lemma 3.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let gij(x,t) be a Ricci flow solution and dt(x,x0) the distance at time t. Suppose Ric ≤ (n−1)K on B_{t0}(x0,r0) (first assertion) or on B_{t0}(x1,r0) (second assertion). Then at t=t0 and outside B_{t0}(x0,r0) one has the differential inequality ∂/∂t d − Δ d ≥ −(n−1)( (2/3)Kr0 + r0^{-1}). A related inequality bounds the time derivative of the distance between two points: d/dt d_t(x0,x1) ≥ −2(n−1)( (2/3)Kr0 + r0^{-1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a parabolic version of a Laplacian/distance comparison: it removes curvature sign restrictions present in the ordinary Laplacian comparison by exploiting Ricci flow evolution. The inequalities are stated in barrier sense if points are conjugate; they are used in maximum-principle arguments controlling the evolution of distance or cutoff functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No local collapsing theorem II (Theorem 3.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any A > 0 there exists κ = κ(A) > 0 with the following property: if gij(t) is a complete Ricci flow solution with bounded curvature on [0,r0^2] and |Rm|(x,t) ≤ r0^{-2} on B_0(x0,r0) × [0,r0^2], and Vol_0(B_0(x0,r0)) ≥ A^{-1} r0^n, then gij(t) is κ-noncollapsed on all scales less than r0 at every point (x,r0^2) with d_1(x,x0) ≤ A r0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This version extends non-collapsing to complete (possibly noncompact) solutions with local bounded curvature, using a cut-off and maximum principle argument. The proof again uses Perelman's reduced volume and the Li–Yau–Perelman distance l(·,τ) and estimates of its minimum via a localized maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: C^∞_loc convergence of tensors on a fixed manifold (concept introduced)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence Ti of tensors on a fixed manifold M converges to T in the C^∞_loc topology if there exists a cover of coordinate charts so that on every compact K contained in charts, the components of Ti converge in C^∞ to the components of T (viewed as functions on R^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard notion of local smooth convergence of tensors; the text emphasizes that C^∞_loc-convergence of metrics on a given manifold differs from convergence of a sequence of marked manifolds because diffeomorphisms can be involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked Riemannian manifold and C^∞_loc convergence of marked balls (Definition 4.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A marking on (M,g) is a choice of a point p∈M; the triple (M,g,p) is a marked Riemannian manifold. A sequence of marked geodesic balls (B(pk,sk),gk,pk) (0<sk≤∞, sk→s) converges in C^∞_loc to a marked (possibly noncomplete) ball (B_∞,g_∞,p_∞) if there exist exhausting open sets U_k ⊂ B_∞ and diffeomorphisms f_k: U_k → V_k ⊂ B(pk,sk) so that the pullback metrics (f_k)^* g_k converge to g_∞ in C^∞ on every compact subset of B_∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is the notion of convergence used for sequences of manifolds (with basepoints) and allows noncompact limits and local convergence without global diameter or injectivity radius hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's Cheeger-type compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (M_k,g_k,p_k) be a sequence of marked complete n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds and consider geodesic balls B(p_k,s_k) with 0<s_k≤∞ and s_k→s (≤∞). Suppose: (a) for every r<s and every integer l≥0 there exist constants B_{l,r} and k(r,l) such that for k≥k(r,l) the curvature tensors and their lth covariant derivatives satisfy |∇^l Rm(g_k)| ≤ B_{l,r} on B(p_k,r); and (b) there exists δ>0 so that inj(M_k,p_k) ≥ δ for all k. Then there exists a subsequence so that (B(p_k,s_k),g_k,p_k) converges in C^∞_loc to a marked geodesic ball (B_∞,g_∞,p_∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement is a local compactness / convergence theorem adapted to allow noncompact limits, avoid global diameter bounds and avoid requiring a uniform injectivity radius lower bound over the entire manifold (only at basepoints). The proof proceeds by choosing coverings by uniformly controlled coordinate charts, bounding overlaps, extracting limits of local coordinate metrics and patching via transition isometries.
